news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire reports 67 vacant surplus former operational assets against a portfolio of 549
news_drafts.lead:
Aberdeenshire Council had 67 vacant surplus former operational assets at the first quarter of 2026/27, according to the Business Services performance report for the Business Services Committee. Its operational portfolio, the buildings and sites it still uses, stands at 549 at the second quarter.

The paper says the number of vacant assets is expected to fall in 2026/27 and 2027/28. A number of closures are planned for early 2027, linked to a new depot and office facility at One Harlaw Road, Inverurie. The performance target for capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is 100% of the amount budgeted.

The committee also has the Business Services budget risk register for 2026/27. It identifies a pressure on income from licensing fees and charges. In the register's words, "Pressure has been identified within Licensing fees and charges however this is currently being offset with underspends across the wider Business Services budget." The risk score for council tax and fees-and-charges collection remains at 16, unchanged, with a residual score of 12.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 – Service response to Internal Audit Report 2710 – ECS Procurement
findings.headline: ECS procurement actions are dated 31 March 2027, with DPA plan milestones from November 2026 to February 2027, and completion is to be confirmed by action owners.
findings.detail: All five recommendations carry a 31 March 2027 timescale. The paper states that completion has not been independently verified, and progress against each action is still to be confirmed by its owner.
findings.matters: The paper reports no completion evidence yet, so whether the 31 March 2027 deadline is met is the test a peer or lender would use to judge whether the remediation landed.
findings.quote: completion has not been independently verified and current progress requires confirmation by action owners.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 – Service response to Internal Audit Report 2710 – ECS Procurement
findings.headline: ECS will review each supplier and framework identified in audit finding 1.3, confirming routes, direct-award approvals and call-off records by 31 March 2027.
findings.detail: Recommendation 1.3, rated Major, requires framework supplier selection to be justified and documented, including call-off records for each separate award. Recommendation 1.4, rated Moderate, covers Contracts Register and Public Contracts Scotland notice completeness.
findings.matters: Gaps in direct-award approvals and call-off records are compliance exposures that a finance director would want to check against their own framework spend.
findings.quote: ECS accepts the findings on procurement routes, supplier selection, approvals and call-off arrangements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 – Service response to Internal Audit Report 2710 – ECS Procurement
findings.headline: The Procurement Approval Form (PAF) threshold changed from £10,000 to £50,000 on 15 January 2026, and ECS will confirm which requirements apply before and after that date.
findings.detail: Recommendation 1.2, rated Major, covers procurement planning, scrutiny and approval. ECS will distinguish historical from current requirements, and the revised Procurement Manual was issued in April 2026.
findings.matters: A change in the approval threshold changes which purchases require a PAF, so a finance director would want to check how the transition was handled against their own thresholds.
findings.figures: £10,000 to £50,000; 15 January 2026; Procurement Manual issued April 2026
findings.quote: including the PAF threshold change from £10,000 to £50,000 on 15 January 2026

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 – Service response to Internal Audit Report 2710 – ECS Procurement
findings.headline: ECS accepts weaknesses in maintaining current Delegated Procurement Authority (DPA) and training records for officers with procurement responsibilities.
findings.detail: Recommendation 1.1, rated Major, covers DPA, training and iProc access. The CPSS DPA Process Review and Improvement Plan proposes electronic applications, renewal reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days before expiry, and quarterly reconciliation of DPA holders against iProc users.
findings.matters: Officers buying without current authority or training is a control gap, and the planned quarterly DPA-to-iProc reconciliation is a specific fix a finance director elsewhere could compare with their own.
findings.figures: renewal reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days before expiry; quarterly DPA/iProc reconciliation; three-year renewals
findings.quote: ECS accepts the identified weaknesses in maintaining current DPA, training records and associated governance arrangements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 – Service response to Internal Audit Report 2710 – ECS Procurement
findings.headline: Internal Audit Report 2710 rates Education and Children's Services procurement as a Major net risk, with Limited assurance at Directorate level.
findings.detail: The draft report, dated 21 August 2026, makes five recommendations on ECS procurement, three rated Major and two rated Moderate. ECS accepts the findings and will lead the improvement work with the Central Procurement Shared Service (CPSS).
findings.matters: A Limited assurance rating at directorate level on procurement is a control weakness that a finance director would want to test against their own procurement assurance.
findings.figures: Major net risk; Limited assurance at Directorate level; 5 recommendations (3 rated Major, 2 rated Moderate)
findings.quote: Overall assessment: Major net risk; Limited assurance at Directorate level.
